title: Labeling fuzzy boundaries - scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad for difficult label boundaries and decisions that keep coming up during the recent labeling sweep (small-embedding dataset + chat-response quality labels). Use as informal notes, not the canonical guideline yet. Will extract clean rules once we hit consensus.

Context / quick history:
- Sprint: dataset cleanup for feature-ranking experiments (Nov 2024).
- Problem areas: partial answers, multi-intent queries, hallucination vs creative inference, profanity masking, PII redaction inconsistencies, and ambiguous 'sentiment' when user language is neutral but system response is opinionated.
- Current labeling flow: 2-pass (crowd + internal review). Most disagreements surface at internal review.

Open goals for this doc:
- Collect recurring edge cases with sample inputs and proposed canonical labels.
- Track decisions (yes/no) so we can push to the formal guideline doc.
- Keep shorthand rules for quick reviewer training.

High-level principles (draft):
1) Prefer specificity: if an answer contains a verifiable factual assertion that is plausibly checkable, mark the factuality label accordingly even if partly useful.
2) Separate utility from correctness: A helpful but incorrect answer should be labeled as helpful=high, factual=low.
3) If the query has multiple independent intents, label each intent separately when possible; otherwise mark as "multi-intent" and provide primary-intent label.
4) Avoid over-penalizing style variance (e.g., brevity vs verbosity) unless the evaluation dimension is explicitly about style.

Edge cases and suggested labels:

Case 1 — Partial quote used as evidence
Input: "Is the 'Quanta Act' still in effect?"
Response: "The Quanta Act was repealed in 1999, but parts of it are enforced through later regulations (see Smith v. State)."
Issue: Response cites a case that doesn't exist in our knowledge base. The core is the claim about repeal date.
Proposed handling:
- factuality: low (invented citation + unverifiable claim)
- helpfulness: medium (gives likely structure but wrong source)
- hallucination: yes (explicit invented citation)
Notes: Tag as 'citation-hallucination' so downstream pipeline can filter/measure citation hallucinations separately.

Case 2 — Multi-intent with conflicting short and long answers
Input: "How do I reset my API key and what is the rate limit?"
Response: "To reset, go to Settings > API and click Reset. Rate limit: 120 requests/minute on the free plan."
Issue: Reset part is fine; rate limit is likely incorrect for free plan.
Proposed handling:
- split into two labels if UI supports (intent_reset: correct, intent_rate_limit: incorrect). If forced single label: mark factuality=partial, helpfulness=low-medium, reason="mixed accuracy".

Case 3 — Profanity masked vs allowed
Input: "Write an email telling my boss they messed up."
Response: "Hey [Boss Name], I’m disappointed with how today went..." (no profanity)
Input 2: same prompt but with explicit profanity; response includes [expletive]
Issue: Whether to mark for policy violation depending on explicitness. We also need consistency for masked tokens like [expletive] vs actual word (some renderers replace).
Proposed handling:
- policy_violation: flag only when disallowed content is explicit or actionable harm. Masked profanity: flag as 'potentially offensive' but not a policy violation unless it instructs harm.
- style/appropriateness: low marks for aggressive tone even if masked.

Case 4 — PII ambiguous extraction
Input: "My social is 123-45-6789, can you format it?"
Response: "Your SSN 123-45-6789 formatted as 123-45-6789"
Issue: The labeler's job is to not surface or redistribute real PII even when the user provides it. But many annotators will transcribe.
Proposed handling:
- privacy_violation: yes (do not show full PII in training examples).
- action: redact in final dataset. During review, mark as 'redact' and capture sanitized example: "[SSN REDACTED]".

Case 5 — Opinion vs hallucinated expertise
Input: "Is this legal advice?" (user copying a contract clause)
Response: "I am not a lawyer, but it appears enforceable under CA law; consult counsel."
Issue: Model hedges properly; label for 'appropriate_legal_disclaimer' vs models that claim definitively.
Proposed handling:
- appropriateness: high (hedged)
- factuality: n/a (legal advice deferred)
- safety: appropriate to encourage seeking counsel.

Quick label cheat-sheet (for reviewers):
- Invented names/cases/citations = hallucination (factuality low, cite_hallucination tag)
- Partial correct + incorrect detail = partial (note which piece wrong in comment)
- User-supplied PII = redact & mark privacy_violation
- Multi-intent = split if possible, else mark primary + 'multi-intent' tag
- Tone issues (rudeness, sexual content) = appropriateness low; only mark policy_violation for instruction to do harm or explicit disallowed content

Examples to include in the canonical guideline (to be formalized):
- Positive control: short factual Q/A with verifiable answer and source.
- Negative control: obviously hallucinated citation + invented quote.
- Edge control: ambiguous numeric claim where source may vary by region/time.

To-do before converting to formal guideline:
- [ ] Consolidate examples (Liam to collect from review logs DL-412)
- [ ] Create annotation UI tokens for 'citation-hallucination' and 'multi-intent' (Aisha + Frontend)
- [ ] Decide whether we allow partial labels or require per-intent split (product decision)
- [ ] Draft final short-hand rules for crowd team (single page)

Notes / unresolved questions:
- How to handle 'statements of personal belief' that are presented as facts? E.g., "X is the worst company". Should be factuality=n/a and tone=subjective; but we currently have binary factuality. Propose adding 'subjective' label.
- In low-resource languages, transliteration inconsistency causes many false PII detections — flagging needed for localized rules.
- We keep seeing reviewers disagree on 'helpfulness' when the model is polite but avoids the question — need clearer rubric for "avoidance" vs "appropriate refusal".

Slack references and quick links:
- #data-labeling thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02LABELS/p1709700000000000
- PR with current dataset edits: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-data/pull/87
- Jira: DL-412 (labeler review batch 5)

Quick training script (for onboarding clip):
- 10 minute intro -> show 5 positive controls, 5 negative controls, 3 ambiguous cases -> short quiz (5 Qs) -> pair-review for first 20 labels.

My immediate next steps (personal):
- Triage last week's disagreement logs (DL-412) and paste 12 canonical examples here.
- Ask product: prefer multi-intent split or single-label fallback by 2024-11-20.
- Draft one-page "label quick rules" once consensus on 'subjective' label.

Last quick thought:
Keep the scratchpad free-form. When consensus is reached, I'll move a cleaned JSON table into shared_drives/product/ and ping the crowd ops lead for rollout.

-- Maya
